analysis: The closest option integrates programming, databases, software construction, algorithms and applied AI with epidemiology, qualitative methods, evidence synthesis and organisational change. The strongest response to clinical information is the overlap in software and data foundations. It lacks a sustained sequence in clinical records, interoperability and healthcare software deployments.

The biomedical option gives mathematical and clinical-context depth through anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, statistics, signal analysis, computer vision and machine learning. Image Processing & Computer Vision moves to term six after Linear Algebra and Linear Systems. The schedule supports general methods and biomedical interpretation without implying clinical diagnosis or validated medical AI.

The health behaviour option builds from introductory psychology and sociology to health psychology, mental health, research and organisational change. Marketing and market research are complementary user-inquiry tools. Added Epidemiology & Public Health, Psychopathology, Medical & Health Psychology and Advanced Research Methods & Statistics to make healthcare and evidence central. The option does not promise clinical practice or production software.

Narrowed comparisons to evidenced partial relationships in software, data, statistics, population health, digital change and image analysis. Left the placement and thesis unpaired and kept optional UCR independent research outside scheduled credits.

alignment.rationale: Both use statistical models and study design. UCR focuses on health and behaviour experiments, while UvA pairs biostatistics with clinical epidemiology.
Both study population health, disease patterns and determinants. UvA connects these topics to its healthcare curriculum.
Both use programming to build working software. UvA applies it to healthcare applications.
Both study organising and retrieving data. UvA addresses how healthcare systems exchange information and knowledge.
Both use logic and formal reasoning. UvA applies these ideas to medical diagnosis.
Both study machine learning. UvA applies AI in the context of healthcare and clinical information.
Both analyse digital images. UCR uses general image-processing and computer-vision methods, while UvA covers medical imaging and signals.
Both develop software design and construction skills. UvA embeds software engineering in medical informatics.
Both develop ideas from user needs and consider how to implement them. UvA focuses on innovation in healthcare.
Both study organisational decisions about technology and change. UvA focuses on information management in healthcare.
